name: City States of Archaic Greece, 650 BC
description: Centuries after the collapse of the Mycenaean culture and the long Dark Age that followed, the people of Greece now reside in fiercely independent poleis - city-states that compete for sacred authority, fertile farmland, and coastal power. The local community is now the center of safety and sovereignty; yet, Greece is still bound by shared gods, language, and a cultural memory of the long-gone heroic age of Achilles. Divided by lineage, geography, and ambition, any polis could expand their authority through conquest, alliances, and trade, uniting the land and restoring unity to all Greeks.
